<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
TypeScript compilation fails because `fast-check` imports from `pure-rand/types/...`, which requires modern moduleResolution. Now considering the cleanest fixes for a VS Code extension.

Adding `"skipLibCheck": true` to tsconfig is the standard fix for VS Code extensions. It skips type checking of declaration files in node_modules. Updating `moduleResolution` to `node16` or `bundler` is another option, though it may conflict with `"module": "commonjs"`. Pinning `fast-check` to an older version is also possible. TypeScript is checking the `.d.ts` file because `src` imports it.

`skipLibCheck: true` is the safest minimal fix for a VS Code extension. It is extremely common in Yeoman generator templates and avoids broader configuration changes. I will add it to tsconfig and verify compilation.
</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Compile succeeds again.

**Cause:** Tests import `fast-check`, whose types pull in `pure-rand/types/...` subpaths. Those only resolve with `moduleResolution` of `node16` / `nodenext` / `bundler`; this project still uses the older default.

**Fix:** Set `"skipLibCheck": true` in `tsconfig.json` so TypeScript does not type-check declaration files under `node_modules` (normal for VS Code extensions).
